why: Rule 1: the 4 cm proton falls monotonically 300k->130k away from the deg-2 junction (stops at 22003) while the 20 cm mu leaves it flat, and the sub-cm blobs sit around this point.
Rule 1 at a clean 4-prong star: zoom shows four arrows in different directions and the 78 cm muon Bragg-rises to 116k at its far end 15000.
Only real object is a 6 cm proton whose dQ/dx falls monotonically 224k->90k from 3000 to 3001, so it stops at 3000 and started at 3001 (rule 1).
Rule 1 with 2 of 2 rising away: 21 cm proton follows the proton template up to 235k at 13003 and the 131 cm muon is hot at 13000, prongs 89 deg apart.

Whole 381 cm cluster is one straight MIP line (principal frame a2,a3 ~ 0), so the mid-track knot of short segments is the only vertex-like structure; I pick 6009 for its 85k proton stub and lower z, but 6005 20 cm away is nearly as good.
Single 181 cm muon with both ends interior; the sustained Bragg rise to 198k over the last 10 cm at 12000 makes that the stopping end, so the vertex is the cool end 12001 (also lower z).
Rule 1 at a 3-prong star: two protons Bragg-rise away (39 cm to 200k, 12.6 cm to 180k) and the muon continues across the cathode as cluster 9 to stop at 9000.
The 400 cm muon starts at this interior deg-3 junction and exits the z=500 face; two short prongs (one with a 200k proton hump) leave the same point, so it is the only interior star.
Rule 1 holds at both 15002 and 15006 (2.6 cm apart); I take 15002 because the 175 cm muon and the 16 cm proton (Bragg to 275k at 15001) both leave it, with Michel-like blobs at the muon stop 15000.
The 101 cm muon starts at this interior point and exits the y=-200 floor with no Bragg, and a 1.7 cm 204k e/cm proton stub hangs off exactly here.

A 354 cm flat-MIP muon running horizontally along +z (beam-like) from this upstream end to the z=500 wall, with a 2.7 cm 144k proton stub at 18009; only caveat is that the point sits 8 cm from the cathode.

Event is only a 2.9 cm 438k proton plus two sub-cm blips, with no p4 profile and identical 5 cm end means so the zoom arrows are red at both ends and carry no direction; I take 17001 because the blips 42005 and 43007 lie on that side, but the two ends are 3 cm apart and I am close to guessing.
Rule 1 plus rule 3: the 78 cm muon Bragg-rises to 225k at 9000 with a Michel-like blob 6 cm off that end, so the cool interior end 9001 is the start.
Rule 1 with 2 of 2 rising away at 120 deg: an 86 cm proton rises to 290k at 14000 and a 151 cm muon rises to 175k at 14001, which also carries the Michel-like blobs of cluster 60.
The 135 cm muon is flat MIP at both ends, so it cannot be stopping; 13000 is on the z=500 wall, leaving the interior end 13001 as the origin, and small blobs sit within 6 cm of it.
